solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: With second being moved on, afraid for cushy job (8)

indicatorNotes.being moved on: the S is lifted out of its place and moved on to the front

blocks.note: s = second, the unit of time
afraid = INSECURE, which gives up its S to the front

annotation.surface: Someone nervous about their prospects is given an easy job once a deputy is moved elsewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: INSECURE and SINECURE share every letter: only the S shifts. 'Second' reads as a deputy being moved on, not a letter changing place.
annotation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post that requires little or no work.

entries.clue: What we’d like you to find in mobile loo units (8)

annotation.definition: What we’d like you to find

indicatorNotes.mobile: mobile letters move around into a new order

annotation.surface: A setter's aside about portable toilets, as if hunting for something in a row of Portaloos.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter speaks straight to the solver: the thing we want you to find is the solution. 'Mobile loo units' looks like a festival toilet block.
annotation.definitionFit: Setters want solvers to find the solution to each clue.

entries.clue: Tend to blaspheme if Catholic turns pagan ultimately (5)

indicatorNotes.turns: the C turns into something else
indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of pagan

blocks.note: C = Catholic, the letter to be replaced
last letter of pagaN replaces the C

annotation.surface: A worry that a believer might swear once they abandon their faith.
annotation.walkthrough: CURSE becomes NURSE when its C (Catholic) is swapped for N. The surface's religious conversion is really one letter changing.
annotation.definitionFit: To tend someone who is ill is to nurse them.

entries.clue: A cute yob riddled with hatred for some of the old set? (7-3,4)

indicatorNotes.riddled: riddled with holes, the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the rest of the fodder, 6 letters, 'with' the first part

annotation.surface: A sweet-looking thug is consumed by loathing for part of the older crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The old set' reads as the older generation; it is an old television set, whose picture came from a cathode-ray tube. The question mark flags that the tube is only part of the set.
annotation.definitionFit: Pre-flatscreen televisions built their picture on a cathode-ray tube, a component of the set.

entries.clue: Regret touring quiet European capital abroad (5)

indicatorNotes.touring: RUE tours round P, going all the way around it

blocks.note: to rue = to regret; it goes round P

annotation.surface: Someone sorry they took a quiet Continental trip round a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city to tour; here it is money, the currency of India and elsewhere. R(P)UE then E.
annotation.definitionFit: The rupee is money used abroad, in India, Pakistan and other countries.

entries.clue: Bloody revolutionary times with resistance at the gates? (4)

indicatorNotes.at the gates: R stands at the entrance, the front of the word

annotation.surface: Violent revolutionary days with fighters resisting at a city's gates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a description of revolution; it is how a steak is cooked. Resistance does not fight here: it is the physics symbol R.
annotation.definitionFit: A bloody steak is a rare one, barely cooked.

entries.clue: Emphasize restraint in the task of engineer (9)

blocks.note: working for something = in the task of it

annotation.surface: A reminder to stress how much care an engineer's work needs.
annotation.walkthrough: Engineers do reinforce things, so the surface sits close to the answer. CE, a civil engineer, is a standard crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: strengthening a point with extra force is emphasizing it.

entries.clue: Way to bottle up rising anger for judge (6)

indicatorNotes.to bottle up: RD holds the other letters inside it, as a bottle does
indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, reversed

blocks.note: RD = road, a way; it goes round the rest

annotation.surface: Advice for a judge on how to keep a mounting temper in check.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts a judge in the courtroom; here judge is a verb, to consider or regard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to judge is to consider or look upon someone in a certain way.

entries.clue: What some wear up in bed is rich green pants (6,8)

indicatorNotes.pants: pants in the British slang sense, rubbish or poorly made, so the letters are a mess

annotation.surface: A remark that some people lie in bed wearing lavish green trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up' is riding in the saddle, not sitting up in bed. 'Pants' looks like the garment and is the indicator: in British slang pants means rubbish.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Up' means in the saddle, and these trousers are a definition by example of what riders wear there.

entries.clue: Music producer when on the spot goes red (6)

indicatorNotes.goes: 'goes' in the sense of departs: the letters it refers to leave the word they were in

blocks.note: IN = on the spot, present; it is removed

annotation.surface: A record producer blushes when put under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a studio boss; it is an instrument. Take IN out of CLARINET to leave CLARET.
annotation.definitionFit: Claret is a deep purplish red, named after the Bordeaux wine.

entries.clue: Supplement giving coverage to broadcasting unions (8)

indicatorNotes.giving coverage to: PS covers the other letters, wrapped round them

blocks.note: PS = postscript, a supplement to a letter

annotation.surface: A newspaper supplement reporting on trade unions in the broadcasting industry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unions' reads as trade unions; it means couplings, pairings.
annotation.definitionFit: A pairing is a union of two things or people.

entries.clue: Clip from gun-fest Yellowstone gets complaint (4)

indicatorNotes.Clip from: a clip is a short extract, here letters lifted from the words

annotation.surface: A trailer from a violent TV western draws a viewer's grumble.
annotation.walkthrough: Yellowstone is an American TV western, so 'clip' reads as a film trailer; it is the extract instruction. 'Complaint' is a medical one.
annotation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor medical complaint.

entries.clue: Give too much dope to extra popular with cast (10)

blocks.note: to cast is to form, as in a mould

annotation.surface: A film extra who is too popular with the rest of the cast gets drugged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' is information, not drugs, and 'extra' and 'cast' pretend to be film talk.
annotation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information or the lowdown, so giving too much of it means telling more than is needed.

entries.clue: On going through the change, be a rugged old character (6,6)

annotation.surface: Advice that menopause will turn you into a tough, weather-beaten old character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The change' is the menopause in the surface, and 'rugged old character' looks like a single phrase; only 'character' is the definition, a printed symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: The double dagger (‡) is a typographic character used for footnotes.

entries.clue: Trouble with one punching linesmen in game (9)

indicatorNotes.punching: a punch goes into something, so ILL + I goes into BARDS

blocks.note: bards are poets, men of lines of verse; they take the rest inside

annotation.surface: Trouble breaks out when a player hits the officials during a match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Linesmen' are football officials in the surface; in the wordplay they are poets, who write lines.
annotation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue game played on a baize table.

entries.clue: One branching out from party after Brexit (3)

indicatorNotes.after Brexit: Brexit read as B-exit: the B leaves the word

blocks.note: a bash is a party; Brexit splits as B + exit, so its B leaves

annotation.surface: A politician strikes out on their own, leaving their party after Brexit.
annotation.walkthrough: Split 'Brexit' as B + exit, an instruction to drop B from BASH. A bash is a party. 'Branching out' sounds like quitting politics; it describes a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: An ash is a tree, something that puts out branches.

entries.clue: Avoiding drinking a little having gained kilo (8)

blocks.note: to sip is to drink a little; K goes in after the S

annotation.surface: Someone cutting down on drink after putting on weight.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a diet; 'kilo' reads as weight gained, and gives only its abbreviation K.
annotation.definitionFit: To skip a class is to avoid it.

entries.clue: Hacker messing with Nestlé’s US servers (12)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, second part; the accent is dropped

annotation.surface: A cyberattack on the computer servers of the food giant's American arm.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining fodder to definition. 'Servers' look like computers; they are people who serve, and leatherneck is slang for a US Marine.
annotation.definitionFit: Leathernecks are US Marines, named for their old leather collars; they serve in the forces.

entries.clue: Third-class paper written about study in outer space? (6)

indicatorNotes.written about: about means turned round, so RAG is written backwards

blocks.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper; reversed
a den is a study, a private room

annotation.surface: A cheap tabloid runs a story about research into the cosmos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outer space' pretends to be the cosmos; the question mark flags a joke: a garden is the space outside the house.
annotation.definitionFit: A garden is the outdoor space belonging to a home.

entries.clue: Wise men panic about Republican official (10)

indicatorNotes.about: STATE goes about, around, the R

blocks.note: the Magi, the wise men of the Nativity
a state = a panic, as in 'getting in a state'; it goes round R

annotation.surface: Sages alarmed by a Republican office-holder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Panic' is a noun here: to be in a state is to be in a panic.
annotation.definitionFit: A magistrate is an official who administers the law.

entries.clue: Get more lines with National Theatre or rep? (5)

blocks.note: to age is to get more lines, wrinkles

annotation.surface: An actor weighing a bigger part at the National Theatre against a spell in repertory.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre surface makes 'lines' a script and 'rep' repertory theatre; lines are wrinkles and a rep is a representative. An actor's agent fits the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A rep, a representative, acts for someone else, as an agent does.

entries.clue: Head of Corps first to authorize exercises (4)

indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of each of Corps and authorize

annotation.surface: The commander of a military corps is the first to approve training drills.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of Corps' reads as a commander; 'Head' alone is the definition, a headland.
annotation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland jutting into the sea.

entries.clue: Men with soldier under cavalry leader Cardigan? (5)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, OR + GI sits under the C
indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of cavalry is its first letter

annotation.surface: Soldiers serving under Lord Cardigan, who led the Charge of the Light Brigade.
annotation.walkthrough: Lord Cardigan led the cavalry at Balaclava, so the surface is military history. The Cardigan is one of the two breeds of Welsh corgi; the question mark marks the example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Cardigan is one of the two Welsh breeds of this short-legged dog, the other being the Pembroke.

entries.clue: Sweet fit to be served after a party with king (8)

indicatorNotes.to be served after: ABLE comes after the other pieces

annotation.surface: A dessert, fit for a king, is brought out after a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as pudding and 'served' continues the meal; sweet is an adjective here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sweet in the sense of charming or lovable, as a small child or puppy is.

entries.clue: Merry mirth steals heart of Valerie Singleton (6)

indicatorNotes.Merry: merry, tipsy, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.steals: MIRTH takes in the stolen letter
indicatorNotes.heart of: the heart of a word is its middle letter

annotation.surface: Laughter steals the heart of Valerie Singleton, presenter of Blue Peter.
annotation.walkthrough: Valerie Singleton presented the British children's programme Blue Peter, so the surface reads as a name; 'Singleton' is the definition, a solitary person.
annotation.definitionFit: A singleton is someone living alone, and a recluse who shuns all company is the extreme case.

entries.clue: My love gets intense on regular occasions (4)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is ONE'S, the possessive, which stands in for 'my' as a generic pronoun

indicatorNotes.on regular occasions: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

annotation.surface: A lover's sigh that their partner gets passionate only now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My love' reads as an endearment; 'My' is the definition, ONE'S, a pronoun as in 'one does one's best'.
annotation.definitionFit: One's is the impersonal possessive, used where a speaker might say my.

entries.clue: Saving time for left in making cuts (8)

indicatorNotes.for: T stands in for L, replacing it

blocks.note: slashing = making cuts; its L is replaced
t = time, which replaces l = left

annotation.surface: Budget talk: time spent economising while the cuts are being made.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a budget round, so 'saving' and 'cuts' sit together naturally; SLASHING swaps its L for T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting money or goods away in a hiding place for later is saving them.
